source.title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; there are minor table and formatting artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates unlearning behavior and utility using a concept-paired benchmark and contextual-separation metric, rather than testing recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper tests behavioral forgetting, benign retention, and contextual separation. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting. Results cited from other work about fine-tuning or removing activation directions are not rows.
record.test_reason: Its own results bear on the first half of version A: whether unlearning removes fine-tuned harmful content while keeping utility on paired benign queries. The setting is new (dual-use concepts, harmful data injected by fine-tuning, LLM-judge behaviour scores). It runs no recovery attacks, so B–F and A's 'simple attacks don't recover it' clause are untested. The contextual-separation metric is the paper's own construct and fits no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also state that adversarial and relearning robustness are out of scope. They cite Łucki et al. that RMU can be undone, but do not test it.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes models on paired harmful and benign data, then evaluates Gradient Ascent, SimNPO, RMU, and UNDIAL on its own benchmark. It does not reproduce recovery attacks or the original studies' attack evaluations.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by method and model; contextual separation also varies across concepts. The paper reports that reducing the forget-set proportion produces only a small increase in contextual separation (Figure 4).

fits_no_version.finding: Contextual separation (HelpScore − HarmScore on paired dual-use concept queries) after unlearning stays well below a retain-only reference (e.g. RMU 0.31 vs 0.62 on Llama). Separation depends more on concept and model than on method.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning methods fail to selectively remove harmful uses of a concept while preserving its benign uses (concept-level contextual separation).

record.problems: One run per setting is stated in the limitations, with shared untuned hyperparameters. The authors note the benchmark is in-distribution and partly measures memorization; harmful and benign data come from different generators, potentially allowing stylistic shortcuts. The evaluator is GPT-5.4 from the benign-data generator's model family. Reference baselines were limited to two models, and Safety SFT uses extra refusal supervision. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 ROUGE results (HarmMem, HarmQA, HelpRet, HelpQA) for methods and models, Appendix Table 8 macro-averaged results, and concept-wise and forget-set-size analyses in Figures 2–4 and Tables 4–5 are not included; the 60-row limit was used for Table 2's judge metrics and Table 3 reference baselines. Table 3's repeated unlearning-method scores are also omitted as duplicates of Table 2.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the removed content. Also near-chance accuracy on pretrained hazardous knowledge: the forgotten content here was injected by fine-tuning and scored by a harm judge, not by accuracy.
No activation ablation or analysis of access vs deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, cross-lingual or in-context attacks.

missing.what: ROUGE results: HarmQA, the content-recall measure closest to A's 'targeted-knowledge' criterion, plus HarmMem, HelpRet and HelpQA. For SimNPO/RMU, HarmQA stays above base in 7 of 8 cases. Declared left out, but needed for A.
Base-model scores (HarmScore 0.06–0.11, HelpScore 0.26–0.44) as the floor for forgetting; rows use only the fine-tuned baseline.

record.verdict_notes: Contradiction in the source: Section 5.2 says each model is averaged over 3 seeds, while Limitations says one run per setting. Unlearning here removes data injected by fine-tuning (moderate-severity harms), not pretrained hazardous knowledge. Scoring is behavioural via a GPT-5.4 judge on in-distribution queries, so A's verdicts apply only to this setting. Paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests behavioral forgetting, helpful retention, and contextual separation for four unlearning methods. Does not test whether simple attacks recover the knowledge, or establish near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy.
No post-unlearning relearning or fine-tuning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or experiment distinguishing blocked access from deletion is conducted.
No prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack is tested.
The evaluated methods are not tested for resistance to the attacks in the claim.

relationships.condition: Gradient Ascent (with retain-set descent), all four models
relationships.reason: Harm drops to base level (q3/q7/q32/l8-ga-harm), but HelpScore falls below the base model (0.08–0.22; q3/q7/q32/l8-ga-help). General ability is not kept.
relationships.display_finding: Harm fell to base levels, but HelpScore dropped below base performance to 0.08–0.22.

relationships.condition: SimNPO and RMU, all four models
relationships.reason: Utility is largely retained (e.g. q3-sim-help 0.48 vs 0.52), but HarmScore stays above base (0.13–0.27 vs 0.06–0.11), so forgetting is incomplete.
relationships.display_finding: Utility was largely retained, including 0.48 versus 0.52, but HarmScore remained 0.13–0.27 versus base levels of 0.06–0.11.

relationships.reason: Forgetting is partial (HarmScore 0.15–0.24) and utility partly lost (0.39–0.48 vs 0.59–0.71 fine-tuned).
relationships.display_finding: UNDIAL retained HarmScore values of 0.15–0.24 while utility fell to 0.39–0.48 from fine-tuned levels of 0.59–0.71.

relationships.reason: HelpScore 0.21 is below the base model (0.33) while harm is only partly reduced (0.19). Utility is not kept.
relationships.display_finding: HelpScore fell to 0.21 versus base 0.33, while harm remained partly reduced at 0.19.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Four tested models and four unlearning methods
reader_labels.reason: Methods reduce harmful scores, but helpful retention and contextual separation remain incomplete or trade off against forgetting; the paper reports separation below the retain-only reference (main method rows, including q3-ga-help, q7-ga-sep, q32-rmu-sep, and l8-rmu-sep).
